::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 9th 1891  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Pusey House WOOD 5/4/1[^1]
:::

Dear [Madam](people/person_1554.qmd)
I am afraid I have not knowledge enough to help you with questions, as books of the kind do not come much in my way.  From what I have heard, [Professor Cheyne](people/person_2103.qmd)’s books would be to be avoided.[^2]  I believe there is one which reduces Elijah’s miracles to myths, but I only heard it discussed, and there are also his interpretations of the Psalms.

I saw the first number of the [Newbery House Magazine](organizations/other_83.qmd).  There the paper on the Psalms, which called the Second not Messianic, was enough for me, so I do not know how they went on, but I rather think the papers were discontinued  It is a very difficult thing to choose safe readings for the Higher Education subjects

yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: With envelope addressed to Miss H. A. Woodgate/Crowthorne/ Wokingham and postmarked illegibly.
[^2]: The Rev. Thomas Kelly Cheyne (1841-1915), Oriel Professor of the Interpretation of Scripture at Oxford (1885-1908).  A.S. Peake in the supplement (1927) to the original DNB observed darkly that his ‘theological position became in his later years more and more indefinite . . .It may . .  be questioned whether at the end he could be regarded as a Christian in any tenable sense of that elastic term . .’
